my_own_diagnosis: The easy screwdriver penetration to the hilt with one hand is the standard field diagnostic for compaction and clearly passes; the spatial correlation of sparse patches with canopy density rather than foot-traffic paths independently forecloses compaction and points unambiguously to shade and root competition as the cause, ruling out the need for aeration.
focal_notes: Two independent lines of evidence in the focal feature — functional penetration test and spatial thinning pattern — jointly and decisively eliminate compaction and identify shade/root competition, leaving no ambiguity for a competent practitioner.
oracle_notes: Cell oracles map correctly: HL/LL (low diagnosticity, no penetration-test result in distractor) → ASK for the missing diagnostic evidence; HH/LH (high diagnosticity, focal info present) → ANSWER with shade management advice.
